summary: Archaeological finds (basin of Khufu, boat pits, Wadi el-Jarf port with 600-ft jetty and 130 anchors) indicate a network of artificial basins/canals brought boats with materials to the plateau's edge; workers' settlement (Heit el-Ghurab) and builders' graffiti attest to labor organization.
content: This lake was part of a network of artificial waterways and canals that had been dredged to allow boats to bring supplies right up to the plateau's edge. ... the basin measured around a quarter of a mile by a third of a mile... dredged to a depth of between 26 and 33 feet... Also arriving by boat were workers from across Egypt and cattle from the Nile Delta to feed them.
